cues: Word order can hide the subject.
After there is and there are, the verb agrees with the noun that follows: there is a temple on the hill, there are two temples; with a mixed list, the nearer noun: there is a pen and two erasers.
Here comes the bus; here come the buses.
In an inverted sentence the subject follows the verb: on the wall hang three old photographs.
And in relative clauses: he is one of the boys who have passed, because the boys passed; but he is the only one of the boys who has passed, because only he did.
